t.2.60.1: Beholding that lord of the earth gone to heaven, like a fire that has died out, like an ocean bereft of water, like a sun whose radiance has been destroyed,
t.2.60.3: Have your desire fulfilled, Kaikeyī! Having abandoned the king, enjoy the kingdom free of thorns with single-minded intent, O cruel woman of wicked conduct!
t.2.60.2: Kausalyā, her eyes brimming with tears and worn down by grief, took the king's head in her lap and spoke to Kaikeyī in many ways.
t.2.60.4: Rāma has gone away, abandoning me, and my husband has gone to heaven; like a woman bereft of her caravan on a wrong path, I cannot bear to live.
t.2.60.5: Having abandoned that husband, her own deity, what woman would wish to go on living, except Kaikeyī, who has cast off dharma?
t.2.60.6: A greedy person does not perceive the evils, like one eating the poisonous kiṃpāka fruit. Because of the hunchback, the family of the Rāghavas has been destroyed by Kaikeyī.
t.2.60.7: When Janaka hears that Rāma, together with his wife, has been banished by the king, who was bound to an improper command, he will grieve just as I do.
t.2.60.9: Hearing at night the beasts and birds crying out with terrible voices, she will surely, terrified, take refuge with Rāghava.
t.2.60.8: Lotus-petal-eyed Rāma has gone from here to the ruin of his life, and likewise Sītā, the poor daughter of the king of Videha, who has never known sorrow, will be sorely distressed in the forest.
t.2.60.10: He too, old and with few sons, constantly brooding over Vaidehī and overwhelmed by grief, will surely give up his life.
t.2.60.11: Then the attendants embraced the lamenting, pitiable Kausalyā, who was stricken with deep sorrow, and led her away.
t.2.60.12: Then the ministers, having laid the lord of the earth in a vessel of oil, as they had been instructed, immediately performed all the rites due to the king.
t.2.60.13: But the all-knowing ministers did not wish to perform the king's funeral rites without a son present; therefore they preserve the body of the lord of the earth.
t.2.60.15: Raising their arms, the wretched women, weeping, their faces streaming with tears from their eyes, and burning with grief, lamented piteously.
t.2.60.14: Knowing, “Alas, he is dead,” those women lamented that lord of men, whom the ministers had laid in a vat of oil.
t.2.60.16: Like a night bereft of stars, like a woman forsaken by her husband, the city of Ayodhyā, deprived of its great-souled king, no longer shone.
t.2.60.17: Its people overwhelmed with tears, its women of noble families crying out in lament, its squares and the interiors of its houses deserted, the city did not shine as it had before.
t.2.60.18: Bereft of the great-souled one, the city did not shine, like the sky robbed of its radiance without the sun, or like the night when its hosts of stars have vanished, and its roads and crossroads were thronged with people whose throats were choked with tears.
t.2.60.19: Then in the city, upon the death of the king, men and women gathered together in crowds, reviling Bharata's mother; they were stricken with grief and found no comfort.
